headline: Cox deal lifts sales; franchise write-down drives loss
summary_short: Charter's Q3 2026 revenue was $14.9 billion, up 9.1% y/y on the Cox deal, but a $6.3 billion franchise impairment pushed net income to a $2.4 billion loss.
summary_long: Actual revenue rose 9.1% y/y, driven by the Cox Transactions; pro forma revenue fell 1.5% on lower residential video and Internet revenue. Adjusted EBITDA grew 6.9% to $5.9 billion on an actual basis. The net loss reflects a $6.3 billion franchise impairment, partly offset by a $1.4 billion gain on debt extinguishment. Pro forma Internet customers fell 233,000 while mobile lines rose 508,000. Free cash flow was $674 million, down $947 million. Charter targets $2 billion of annualized opex savings over 18 months, on top of more than $1 billion of Cox synergies.
confidence_notes: Release gives both actual and pro forma figures; KPIs shown are actual (Cox consolidated from close), so y/y growth is inflated by the acquisition. Shard EPS (-20.50) matches the release's basic loss per share. Operating income y/y uses shard SEC values. Debt and cash figures are from shard SEC XBRL, not re-read in the release. No numeric guidance given beyond the cost-savings target.
